body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

fountain_toss | Narrator | - | The coin sinks, and warmth settles on each shoulder. One sentence.
fountain_take_ok | Narrator | - | The party fills a pocket with wishes and nothing happens. One sentence.
fountain_take_cursed | Narrator | - | Cold coin, and a cold feeling in the stomach; the fountain remembers. One sentence.
urn_study | Narrator | - | Rows of clay urns line the walk; some of them hum a thin, terrible note. One sentence.
urn_study_ok | Narrator | - | The humming urns are mourning urns, and they wail if they are opened; one stands silent, with owls on its side. One or two sentences.
urn_study_plain | Narrator | - | The humming is unsettling and the party cannot say why. One sentence.
urn_wrong | Narrator | - | The urn hums a mourning note that rises as a hand nears the lid. One sentence.
urn_warn | Narrator | - | This is a mourning urn: opening it will wail. One short sentence.
urn_wrong2 | Narrator | - | The urn hums a mourning note that rises as a hand nears the lid. One sentence.
urn_wail_ok | Narrator | - | The urn wails, and the party hears it as a wave and lets it pass. One sentence.
urn_wail_fail | Narrator | - | The wail goes through everyone like a hand through water, and every hero staggers. One sentence.
urn_empty | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says not that one; the loud ones hold only ash. Two short sentences.
urn_right | Narrator | - | The urn with owls on its side is silent; it does not wail. One sentence.
urn_right_open | Narrator | - | Inside the silent urn lies a single barn owl feather, white as a new moon. One sentence.
lavender | Narrator | - | A bed of lavender gone wild; the party picks a bunch. One sentence.
lilies | Narrator | - | White lilies bloom in the rain; the party picks a few. One sentence.
amber_find | Narrator | - | Amber lights bob in the fog, leading nowhere the party can follow; the brazier is somewhere among them. One sentence.
amber_found | Narrator | - | The lights circle one hollow, and the brazier of orange coals is in it. One sentence.
amber_pit_ok | Narrator | - | An hour is lost in the fog, and the edge of a mass grave catches no one; Yorgrim's lantern then finds the brazier. Two sentences.
amber_pit_fail | Narrator | - | The ground gives way into a mass grave and skeletal hands pull, until the party tears free; then Yorgrim's lantern finds the brazier. Two sentences.
amber_yorgrim | Narrator | - | Yorgrim raises his lantern and the amber lights scatter, showing the brazier. One sentence.
mass_grave | Narrator | - | The edge of a mass grave yawns, and skeletal hands stir at the bottom of it. One sentence.
grave_study | Narrator | - | Crows flock on one post in the field. One short sentence.
grave_study_ok | Narrator | - | The crows ring one shallow grave to the east; it holds the straw. One or two sentences.
grave_study_plain | Narrator | - | The crows are no help at all. One sentence.
grave_dig | Narrator | - | The party starts to dig the shallow grave; carrion birds explode out of the ground. One sentence.
grave_dig2 | Narrator | - | The party starts to dig the shallow grave; carrion birds explode out of the ground. One sentence.
grave_birds_ok | Narrator | - | The birds scatter and the grave under them holds nothing but a bone or two. One sentence.
grave_birds_fail | Narrator | - | The birds' wings are thick with grave-dust and the party coughs for a while. One sentence.
grave_empty | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says this one holds no straw, and a pale shape stirs in the fog. Two short sentences.
grave_right | Narrator | - | The crows gather thickest on this grave. One short sentence.
grave_right_dig | Narrator | - | A dry bundle of straw lies in the shallow grave, tied with a bit of blue yarn. One sentence.
muck | Narrator | - | Acrid muck seeps up between the tiles of the lane and stings the nose. One sentence.
muck_ok | Narrator | - | The party picks a dry way over the slick tiles. One sentence.
result:
fountain_toss: The coin sinks through the black water with a soft plink, and a quiet warmth like hearth-smoke settles on your shoulders.
fountain_take_ok: You scoop a handful of wet copper into your pocket, and the still dark water does not stir.
fountain_take_cursed: The wet coins sit like river-ice in your palm, and a sour, sinking cold knots in the pit of your stomach.
urn_study: Rows of damp clay urns line the mossy walk, and several of them hum a thin, reed-like note that sets your teeth on edge.
urn_study_ok: These humming vessels are mourning urns, bound to wail if their seals are broken. Only one pot sits quiet at the end of the row, painted with pale barn owls.
urn_study_plain: The thin, droning hum vibrates through the soles of your boots, though you cannot tell what stirs inside the clay.
urn_wrong: The clay urn vibrates under your fingertips, its mournful hum rising to a sharp pitch as your hand nears the waxed lid.
urn_warn: That is a mourning urn, and breaking its seal will loose a bitter wail.
urn_wrong2: The low drone inside the vessel climbs to a shrill whine as your fingers brush the cold clay rim.
urn_wail_ok: A reed-thin shriek pours from the open mouth of the urn, washing past your ears like a cold wave before fading into the fog.
urn_wail_fail: The keening wail passes right through your ribs like an icy hand through water, leaving the whole party staggering on the wet stones.
urn_empty: Leave that clay alone, travelers. The loud ones hold only grey ash and old grief.
urn_right: The urn painted with pale barn owls sits cool and silent beneath your hand.
urn_right_open: Nestled in the dry dust at the bottom of the pot lies a single barn owl feather, white as a new moon.
lavender: A tangled bed of wild lavender grows against the iron fence, and you snap off a fistful of the sharp, sweet-smelling stems.
lilies: Rain-heavy white lilies nod in the ditch, and you gather a few cold, waxy blooms by their wet stems.
amber_find: Pale amber lights bob through the wet heather like stray sparks, leading your eyes in circles while the iron brazier hides somewhere in the mist.
amber_found: The drifting amber lights wheel around a muddy hollow, where a dark iron brazier sits heaped with cold orange coals.
amber_pit_ok: You tramp for a bleak hour through the mire,skirts brushing the crumbled lip of an open mass grave without slipping in. At last, the pale beam of the hound's lantern cuts the fog and catches the iron ribs of the brazier.
amber_pit_fail: The rotten sod gives way beneath your boots and drops you into a pit where dry, skeletal fingers claw at your cloaks until you haul yourselves out of the mud. Ahead in the mist, the pale lantern finally gleams against the dark iron of the brazier.
amber_yorgrim: The old orc lifts the hooded lantern high, and the false amber lights scatter like moths to leave the iron brazier plain in the gloom.
mass_grave: The sodden earth drops away into a yawning trench, where pale bone fingers twitch and scrape in the black mud at the bottom.
grave_study: A murder of wet-feathered crows huddles shoulder to shoulder atop a single crooked fencepost.
grave_study_ok: Every black beak points east toward one sunken mound in the nettles. If any grave holds dry straw, it is that one.
grave_study_plain: The wet crows only cock their heads and rasp at you from the rotting post, offering no sign at all.
grave_dig: No sooner does your spade bite into the wet turf than the mound bursts open in a shrieking cloud of black carrion birds.
grave_dig2: Your shovel strikes the shallow earth, and a tangle of greasy black wings erupts from the soil into your faces.
grave_birds_ok: You duck as the frantic wings beat past your ears, leaving naught in the shallow pit but a few cracked ribs of bone.
grave_birds_fail: The beating wings choke the air with sour grave-dust, leaving you bent double and coughing grit from your lungs.
grave_empty: There is no straw under that sod, only cold mud. Keep your blades ready, for something pale is stirring in the mist.
grave_right: The black crows crowd thickest around the head of this sunken mound.
grave_right_dig: Just beneath the wet roots lies a dry bundle of golden straw, neatly bound with a faded scrap of blue yarn.
muck: Black, sour muck oozes up between the cracked flagstones of the lane, stinging your nostrils with the reek of old rot.
muck_ok: You step from one high stone to the next, keeping your boot-heels clear of the slick black ooze.
